SCHENGEN 90/180 DAY CALCULATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

How many Schengen days do you have left, and when must you leave?

Paste your past stays, pick the date to check from, and optionally a planned entry date. You get days used and left in the rolling 180 days, when allowance returns, and your longest possible trip with the last permitted exit day.

Written from the published 90/180 rule without a live lookup. Border practice and member states change; the official calculator and the border authority decide. Not legal or immigration advice.

What it does, and what it leaves to you

    
    
      
  • Covers: the 90-days-in-any-180 rule with entry and exit days counted, overlapping stays merged, history that already exceeds the limit, and the longest stay from a planned entry date.
    • 
      
  • Gives: days used and left, when days drop out of the window, last permitted exit and the earliest entry for a trip length.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: long-stay (type D) visas, residence permits, bilateral visa waiver agreements that allow longer stays, which countries currently belong to Schengen, how an officer reads your passport stamps or EES record, and ETIAS conditions. Your border authority or consulate decides these.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Common questions

    
Do I need to check my Schengen days before a trip?

    
Yes. Short-stay visitors may spend at most 90 days in any rolling 180-day period in the Schengen area. Overstaying can lead to fines, entry bans and visa refusals.

    
Do the days of entry and exit count?

    
Yes. Both the day you enter and the day you leave count as full days of stay.

    
Which countries count?

    
The Schengen states. Ireland, Cyprus and the United Kingdom are outside it, so time there does not count. Check the current member list, which has changed over time.

    
How does the rolling 180 days work?

    
For any day, look back 179 days plus that day. Count your days in the area in that window. If it is more than 90, you are over. Days drop out as the window moves forward, which is how your allowance returns.

    
Is my data uploaded anywhere?

    
No. Everything is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent.
